arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Richard Friedman argued for Hammon. He said her statements were accusatory. He claimed they satisfied the definition of testimony.
Michael Fisher argued for Indiana. He said the statements were emergency reports. He compared them to 911 calls.
Justice Alito questioned the nature of 911 calls. He asked if they are always testimonial.
Justice Breyer challenged the state's broad definition. He worried it excludes too much evidence.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Amy Hammon told police officers about a domestic violence incident. Indiana prosecutors used her statements at trial. She argues these statements were testimonial. The state argues they were emergency reports. The Court must define the line between these two types of statements.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Hammon wants the Court to rule that her statements were testimonial. She wants the state to exclude them from evidence.
Indiana wants the Court to rule that her statements were non-testimonial. It wants to admit them as evidence.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Hammon argues her statements were made to build a case. She claims this makes them testimonial under the Constitution.
Indiana argues her statements were made to address an emergency. It claims this makes them non-testimonial.
